description: Use this when the user needs a site's raw HTTP response (a JSON API, a form POST, a page exactly as served) rather than scrape's Markdown. Sends the request (method, headers, body) from a residential IP with a browser-compatible TLS profile and returns status, headers, body (bodyBase64 for binary) and finalUrl. A GET or HEAD the site refuses is retried from another IP and, for GET, once in a headless browser; other methods get exactly one attempt. If the site still refuses, the response is marked `blocked` with the reason (`blockClass`, `vendor`) instead of being reported as a success; captchas are never solved. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE can change or delete data on the target site. Use it only for sites and data the user is permitted to access.

auto_render.description: false: never retry a refused GET in the headless browser (default true)

body.description: Request body as a UTF-8 string (JSON, form data, …)

cookies.description: Cookies to send as name→value (e.g. a consent cookie). Only send cookies the user provided for this site.

country.description: ISO country code for the proxy exit, e.g. 'us'

fail_on_block.description: true: a request the site still refuses is returned as an error (HTTP 502) instead of a 200 payload with blocked: true

headers.description: Headers your own client would send. Browser identity headers (User-Agent, Accept, Sec-Fetch-*) are set to match the TLS profile unless keep_headers is set; auth, cookie, content-type and custom headers are forwarded as given.

keep_headers.description: Send your own identity headers verbatim instead of the fingerprint's

method.description: HTTP method (default GET). Only GET/HEAD are retried and escalated: any other method gets exactly one attempt.

render.description: Run the page in a headless browser instead of the TLS tier (GET only): 'html' returns the rendered DOM, 'png' a screenshot in bodyBase64

return_cookies.description: Return the cookies set by the origin as name→value in payload.cookies

session_id.description: Sticky session id — reuse it across calls to keep the same exit IP

success_status_codes.description: Origin statuses to accept as success: never treated as a block, never retried, relayed as-is (e.g. [404])

tier.description: Exit network: premium (default, residential) or mobile. Each tier bills its own prepaid unlocker balance.

timeout_ms.description: Per-attempt timeout at the target, in ms

tls_profile.description: Browser TLS profile for the connection (default chrome)

wait_for_selector.description: With render: wait for this CSS selector before capturing the page

wait_ms.description: With render: extra wait after load, in ms

name: unlock
